====== Request public records from a Virginia public body ======

**Virginia · How do I request public records?** · state model checked by Claude · quality 1.00

//Generated by [[https://github.com/alibama/lexflow|lexflow]] from the state statutes (open-us-law, government publisher text) and checked by Claude: every quoted phrase was matched word for word against the statute text, and the process passed the BPMN/DMN schemas, bpmnlint and a Petri-net soundness check. Information, not legal advice.//

**Governing law:** [[https://law.lis.virginia.gov/vacode/2.2-3704/|Va. Code Ann. § 2.2-3704]] — Public records to be open to inspection; procedure for requesting records and responding to request; charges; transfer of records for storage, etc

  <bpmn:collaboration id="collab_va_records" name="Request public records from a Virginia public body">
    <bpmn:documentation textFormat="text/plain">A Virginia citizen, or media circulating or broadcasting in Virginia, asks a public body for public records</bpmn:documentation>
    <bpmn:extensionElements>
      <lex:model id="va-records" jurisdiction="va" jurisdictionName="Virginia" reviewStatus="draft" method="gold-manual">
        <lex:gap>Subsection E: failure to respond "shall be deemed a denial of the request and shall constitute a violation of this chapter." Both response deadlines route their timers (consequence 'deemed-denial') to the end state deemed_denied, kept separate from a written withholding or not-found response (no_records_released). For the five-working-day deadline this follows E directly. For the B.4 extension it is an inference: a written B.4 response has already been given when that timer runs, and deemed denial is read from E together with B.4's requirement to provide "one of the four preceding responses" within the extension. Enforcement by petition for mandamus or injunction under Va. Code § 2.2-3713 is not modelled.</lex:gap>
        <lex:gap>Subsection A opens records to citizens of the Commonwealth and to representatives of newspapers and magazines circulating, and radio and television stations broadcasting, in or into Virginia; this section grants no right to anyone else, and whether a body answers other requesters is not stated here.</lex:gap>
        <lex:gap>This is the Virginia process, so it governs Charlottesville and other Virginia localities only; requests to the District of Columbia (D.C. Code § 2-532) or to Baltimore (Md. Code, General Provisions § 4-203) follow their own statutes and are modelled separately.</lex:gap>
        <lex:gap>Optional steps that would rejoin the main path are not modelled as separate steps: the custodian may require the requester's name and legal address (A); the cost-estimate exchange tolls the clock, and the request is deemed withdrawn if the requester does not answer an estimate within 30 days (F); a deposit may be required when charges are likely to exceed $200 (H); and unpaid bills 30 days or more past due may have to be paid first (I).</lex:gap>
        <lex:gap>Court petition (C): the condition extraordinary_burden_and_intends_petition stands for both statutory prongs (an extraordinary volume of records or an extraordinarily lengthy search, and a timely response would prevent the body from meeting its operational responsibilities) plus the body's choice to petition, since the agreement duty applies only before proceeding with the petition. The path is an exclusive alternative to the ordinary response and ends at filing; the statute does not say what follows an agreement or the court's ruling.</lex:gap>
        <lex:gap>Extension (B.4): the extra time is available only if the B.4 response is made within five working days, which the model reflects by reaching respond_extended only from a timely respond. The text says 'an additional seven work days' without saying whether they run from the end of the five-day period or from the B.4 response; the timer is a boundary event on respond_extended, so it runs from the B.4 response, which can be shorter than seven work days counted from the end of the five-day period. Criminal investigative files (§ 2.2-3706.1) get 60 work days instead; the timer shows only the seven-day figure.</lex:gap>
        <lex:gap>Subsection F's opening exception for scholastic records under § 2.2-3705.4 A 1 qualifies the permission to make charges; the text does not say whether the later duty to notify the requester of charges before a search still applies to such requests, so notify_charges is shown without a condition.</lex:gap>
        <lex:gap>No new record need be created (D), electronic records must be produced in a medium the body regularly uses (G), and a body that transferred records for storage remains their custodian (J); these shape the response but are not separate steps.</lex:gap>
        <lex:gap>The first response and the B.4 extended response rejoin as exclusive merges: supply and no_records_released are each modelled once and reached from whichever response was given (join 'any'); both missed deadlines lead to the single deemed_denied end state. no_records_released cites B.1 but also covers the B.3 not-found response.</lex:gap>

    <bpmn:exclusiveGateway id="deemed_denied_merge" gatewayDirection="Converging">

===== Steps and the words they come from =====

  - **Request records with reasonable specificity** — Requester (citizen of the Commonwealth, or media circulating or broadcasting in Virginia) · //obligation// (§ 2.2-3704(B)) \\ “//A request for public records shall identify the requested records with reasonable specificity.//”
  - **Notify of charges; offer cost estimate** — Public body (records custodian) · //obligation// (§ 2.2-3704(F)) \\ “//Prior to conducting a search for records, the public body shall notify the requester in writing that the public body may make reasonable charges//”
  - **Try to agree on production with requester** — Public body (records custodian) · //obligation// (§ 2.2-3704%%(C)%%) \\ “//Before proceeding with the petition, however, the public body shall make reasonable efforts to reach an agreement with the requester//”
  - **Petition court for more time** — Public body (records custodian) · //permission// (§ 2.2-3704%%(C)%%) \\ “//Any public body may petition the appropriate court for additional time to respond to a request for records when the request is for an extraordinary volume of records or requires an extraordinarily lengthy search//”
  - **Provide records or answer in writing** — Public body (records custodian) · within 5 business days · //obligation// (§ 2.2-3704(B)) \\ “//provide the requested records to the requester or make one of the following responses in writing//”
  - **Supply inspection or copies at lowest cost** — Public body (records custodian) · //obligation// (§ 2.2-3704(F)) \\ “//shall make all reasonable efforts to supply the requested records at the lowest possible cost//”
  - **Provide records or answer within extension** — Public body (records custodian) · within 7 business days · //obligation// (§ 2.2-3704(B)(4)) \\ “//in which to provide one of the four preceding responses//”

===== Which written response does the public body give? =====

Decision table (DMN), hit policy FIRST.

^ Possible to answer within five work days ^ Records exist and can be found ^ All requested records are exempt ^ Some requested records are exempt ^ → Written response ^ → Takes the extension ^ → Some records are provided ^ Source ^
| false | - | - | - | Not practically possible within five work days; conditions stated | true | false | § 2.2-3704(B)(4) |
| true | false | - | - | Records could not be found or do not exist; contact information for the other public body if known | false | false | § 2.2-3704(B)(3) |
| true | true | true | - | Entirely withheld; volume, subject matter and Code sections cited | false | false | § 2.2-3704(B)(1) |
| true | true | false | true | Provided in part, withheld in part; subject matter of withheld portions and Code sections cited | false | true | § 2.2-3704(B)(2) |
| true | true | false | false | Provide the records | false | true | § 2.2-3704(B) |

===== Which response does the public body give within the extension? =====

Decision table (DMN), hit policy FIRST.

^ Records exist and can be found ^ All requested records are exempt ^ Some requested records are exempt ^ → Response ^ → Some records are provided ^ Source ^
| false | - | - | Records could not be found or do not exist; contact information for the other public body if known | false | § 2.2-3704(B)(3) |
| true | true | - | Entirely withheld; volume, subject matter and Code sections cited | false | § 2.2-3704(B)(1) |
| true | false | true | Provided in part, withheld in part; subject matter of withheld portions and Code sections cited | true | § 2.2-3704(B)(2) |
| true | false | false | Provide the records | true | § 2.2-3704(B) |

===== What the text leaves open =====

  * Subsection E: failure to respond "shall be deemed a denial of the request and shall constitute a violation of this chapter." Both response deadlines route their timers (consequence 'deemed-denial') to the end state deemed_denied, kept separate from a written withholding or not-found response (no_records_released). For the five-working-day deadline this follows E directly. For the B.4 extension it is an inference: a written B.4 response has already been given when that timer runs, and deemed denial is read from E together with B.4's requirement to provide "one of the four preceding responses" within the extension. Enforcement by petition for mandamus or injunction under Va. Code § 2.2-3713 is not modelled.
  * Subsection A opens records to citizens of the Commonwealth and to representatives of newspapers and magazines circulating, and radio and television stations broadcasting, in or into Virginia; this section grants no right to anyone else, and whether a body answers other requesters is not stated here.
  * This is the Virginia process, so it governs Charlottesville and other Virginia localities only; requests to the District of Columbia (D.C. Code § 2-532) or to Baltimore (Md. Code, General Provisions § 4-203) follow their own statutes and are modelled separately.
  * Optional steps that would rejoin the main path are not modelled as separate steps: the custodian may require the requester's name and legal address (A); the cost-estimate exchange tolls the clock, and the request is deemed withdrawn if the requester does not answer an estimate within 30 days (F); a deposit may be required when charges are likely to exceed $200 (H); and unpaid bills 30 days or more past due may have to be paid first (I).
  * Court petition %%(C)%%: the condition extraordinary_burden_and_intends_petition stands for both statutory prongs (an extraordinary volume of records or an extraordinarily lengthy search, and a timely response would prevent the body from meeting its operational responsibilities) plus the body's choice to petition, since the agreement duty applies only before proceeding with the petition. The path is an exclusive alternative to the ordinary response and ends at filing; the statute does not say what follows an agreement or the court's ruling.
  * Extension (B.4): the extra time is available only if the B.4 response is made within five working days, which the model reflects by reaching respond_extended only from a timely respond. The text says 'an additional seven work days' without saying whether they run from the end of the five-day period or from the B.4 response; the timer is a boundary event on respond_extended, so it runs from the B.4 response, which can be shorter than seven work days counted from the end of the five-day period. Criminal investigative files (§ 2.2-3706.1) get 60 work days instead; the timer shows only the seven-day figure.
  * Subsection F's opening exception for scholastic records under § 2.2-3705.4 A 1 qualifies the permission to make charges; the text does not say whether the later duty to notify the requester of charges before a search still applies to such requests, so notify_charges is shown without a condition.
  * No new record need be created (D), electronic records must be produced in a medium the body regularly uses (G), and a body that transferred records for storage remains their custodian (J); these shape the response but are not separate steps.
  * The first response and the B.4 extended response rejoin as exclusive merges: supply and no_records_released are each modelled once and reached from whichever response was given (join 'any'); both missed deadlines lead to the single deemed_denied end state. no_records_released cites B.1 but also covers the B.3 not-found response.
